proposal.hypothesis: LiBr is a wide-gap halide that shares the Li-halide chemistry of Li6PS5Cl. The chloride coatings (Li2MgCl4, Li2ZnCl4) gave the lowest contact penalties so far (0.189 eV/atom, bin 9), while oxide, phosphate, borate and fluoride coatings all reacted more strongly. Halide-halide exchange with the electrolyte should produce less reactive products than P-O or S-O pathways, though Br- is more oxidizable than Cl-, so the 4.0 V stability against LiCoO2 is a risk.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating oxide that is strongly Li-rich. Its O2- anion is already in an unreactive, fully lithiated state, so it should have less driving force to reduce or exchange with the Li6PS5Cl sulfide than the P-O, B-O, or F-based coatings that gave 0.31 to 0.73 eV/atom penalties. It is also expected to be stable against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. This family (simple lithium oxide) has not been tested yet.
